questions.detail: Will the first published U.S. 10-year Treasury constant-maturity yield (FRED DGS10) for 2026-10-05 be above 5.24 percent?

forecasts.rationale: Official Treasury par curve (source of DGS10) shows 10y at 5.28 on 2026-10-02 (5.24 on 10-01; 5.29 peak 09-30). One CNBC headline summary claimed 5.18 after the payrolls miss, conflicting with the official print; I weight the official 5.28 ~90%. Starting 4bp above threshold, with ~5bp daily vol (20d realized 5.2bp) over 1 trading day(s), a random walk gives ~0.71; shaded down for the conflicting report and for mean-reversion risk after the weak September payrolls cut October hike odds to ~17-21%. Probability decays with horizon. Confidence: medium; a single-day move of 4bp or more is common, so this is close to a coin flip with a positive tilt.

forecasts.rationale: The last three first prints were 198k, 198k and 197k (4-week average 200k; consensus last week was 200k). The threshold sits right at the current level, and a 197k print resolves NO. Layoffs remain low, while payroll growth is weak. questions.detail: Will the first published U.S. 10-year Treasury constant-maturity yield (FRED DGS10) for 2026-10-12 be above 5.24 percent?

forecasts.rationale: DGS10 printed 5.24% on Oct 1 (H.15) after a sharp September climb to multi-decade highs, and the market 10-year closed near 5.28% on Oct 2 despite a weak September payrolls report, leaving the level a few basis points above the 5.24% threshold. With roughly a week of trading and recent daily moves of 5-10bp, the outcome is near a coin flip tilted slightly toward above; weaker jobs data trims Fed-hike pressure while FOMC minutes and supply concerns keep upside risk. Oct 12 is Columbus Day, when SIFMA recommends a full bond-market close, so DGS10 will most likely have no value and the question should resolve as cancelled; this probability is conditional on a value being published.

questions.detail: Will the first published U.S. CPI year-over-year inflation (FRED CPIAUCNS) for 2026-09 be above 3.3 percent year over year?

forecasts.rationale: Aug CPI-U NSA 334.980 (3.4% YoY); Sep-2025 base 324.800. Cleveland Fed nowcast (Oct 2) is +0.53% m/m and 3.60% YoY; Street consensus is 3.7%; Nowflation 3.58-3.60%. Weekly retail gasoline averaged ~$4.36 in September vs ~$4.06 in August (+7%), so a large energy contribution is near-certain. Staying at or below 3.3% needs NSA m/m below ~0.2%, which is implausible given the gasoline jump. Confidence: high.

questions.detail: YES if, by 2026-11-10 23:59 ET, USTR publishes a press release on ustr.gov or a Federal Register notice extending the exclusion for 'Printed circuit assemblies for rendering images onto computer screens ("graphics processing modules")' to any date after 2026-11-10. This is entry 20(ttt)(iii)(108) in USTR's exclusion index. USTR describes the current extension as running 'until November 10, 2026'; some secondary notices give the end as 11:59 p.m. EDT on 2026-11-09. Either way, an extension published by 2026-11-10 23:59 ET counts. NO if the exclusion lapses without such an extension. A reinstatement published after 2026-11-10 does not count, even if retroactive.

forecasts.rationale: The 178 exclusions (including graphics processing modules) were extended to 2026-11-10 explicitly 'pursuant to' the Nov 2025 Busan deal. On ~Sep 23 2026 Bessent announced that the Busan Agreement is extended to Jan 10, 2027, so a matching exclusion extension is the default path. USTR has published every prior extension of this set before expiry (May 2025, Aug 2025, Nov 26 2025), though often within days of the deadline. Residual risks are late publication after Nov 10, the GPU line being dropped from a trimmed list, or truce breakdown. Confidence: medium-high; the main risk is timing or format.

questions.detail: YES if, by 2026-12-31, Moore Threads announces through its official website or official social-media accounts that a Lushan-based consumer or gaming graphics card is on sale (orders accepted with a stated price and shipping) to the general public. The same applies if Tom's Hardware reports it as purchasable at retail by that date. Pre-order or reservation sign-ups without shipping, engineering samples and enterprise-only products do not count. Otherwise NO.

forecasts.rationale: On its Sep 3 2026 earnings call Moore Threads said Lushan-related GPU products are 'expected to launch within the year' (有望于年内上市), but was explicitly non-committal on whether a consumer card comes first. Chinese coverage frames Lushan as closer to a pro graphics card (up to 64GB). In its favour, the MTT S80 went on JD.com retail sale almost immediately after its Nov 2022 announcement. Against it, hedged language, a late-December launch slipping retail into 2027, or a pro-first SKU would all resolve NO. Confidence: low.

questions.detail: YES if NVIDIA announces, between 2026-10-03 and 2027-01-31 inclusive, at least one desktop GeForce RTX 50-series card with 'SUPER' in its name, together with a US price or MSRP. The announcement must be made via the NVIDIA Newsroom, NVIDIA GeForce News, or an official NVIDIA keynote backed by such a post. Leaks, partner listings, retailer listings and media reports do not count. Otherwise NO.

forecasts.rationale: Reporting through Jul-Aug 2026 (TrendForce, Benchlife via TweakTown) converges on a CES 2027 (early January) announcement, which falls inside the window, and NVIDIA's GeForce News launch posts normally carry US MSRPs (as with the RTX 40 SUPER at CES 2024). However, the refresh has already slipped repeatedly (CES 2026, then Q2, then Q3, then 'indefinitely'). The blocker, 3GB GDDR7 at $60-70 per module diverted to AI parts, persists, and as of mid-September NVIDIA has not acknowledged the cards exist. Confidence: low; this hinges on one event (CES 2027) and on unresolved memory-supply economics.

questions.title: Will NVIDIA officially announce at least one GeForce RTX 50 'SUPER' desktop graphics card with a US price between 2026-10-03 and 2027-01-31?

questions.detail: YES if, between 2026-10-03 and 2027-03-31, NVIDIA states a US MSRP or 'starting at' price above the launch MSRP for any existing RTX 50 desktop card. Launch MSRPs: 5090 $1,999; 5080 $999; 5070 Ti $749; 5070 $549; 5060 Ti 16 GB $429; 5060 Ti 8 GB $379; 5060 $299; 5050 $249. Qualifying channels: the NVIDIA Newsroom, NVIDIA GeForce News, an NVIDIA US product page, or an NVIDIA statement quoted by Reuters or Bloomberg. Increases only to partner 'kit' prices, retail or marketplace listings, or prices outside the US do not count. Otherwise NO.

forecasts.rationale: NVIDIA has raised partner GPU-kit prices three times in 2026 (Jan, May, ~20-30% later) because of GDDR7 costs, yet it has kept official US MSRPs unchanged. It even sold Founders Editions at launch MSRP at QuakeCon and PAX West in Aug-Sep 2026, while street prices run far above MSRP (RTX 5090 median about $5,000). NVIDIA appears to prefer letting kit and retail prices absorb costs. The main tail is a formal reset around a SUPER launch or a further memory spike. Confidence: medium-low.

questions.detail: YES if an official announcement published in the window raises the US MSRP of at least one of these models above its level on 2026-10-03: PS5 $649.99; Xbox Series X 1 TB $799.99; Switch 2 $499.99. Qualifying channels: the PlayStation Blog, Xbox Wire / news.xbox.com, or Nintendo of America news. Price changes only for bundles, new SKUs, retailers or non-US markets do not count. Otherwise NO.

forecasts.rationale: All three just raised US prices: PS5 to $649.99 (Apr 2 2026), Series X to $799.99 (Aug 1 2026), Switch 2 to $499.99 (Sep 1 2026). The base rate across 2025-26 is about 6-7 US hikes in roughly 18 months across the three firms, with Sony's gap ~8 months and Microsoft's ~3-10 months. AI-driven DRAM/NAND pressure is expected to persist into 2027. Fresh hikes and the US-China tariff truce extension reduce near-term pressure, but a 9-month window across three makers keeps this near even. Confidence: low-medium.
